extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of art criticism; educated general readers interested in painting and aesthetics
extracted.subtask_description: Aesthetic criteria and critical guidance for judging paintings (especially Renaissance and Venetian work), emphasizing pictorial qualities such as sensuous material, drawing, colouring, unity of form and matter, and the relation of subject to pictorial design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique sensuous material of each art
rubrics_metrics.description: The sensuous element in art, and with it almost everything in art that is essentially artistic, is made a matter of indifference; the sensuous material of each art brings with it a special phase or quality of beauty, untranslatable into the forms of any other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism must recognise that each art modality (painting, music, poetry, etc.) has its own incommunicable sensuous charm and special mode of reaching the imagination. Do not evaluate a painting by standards native to music or poetry; instead assess how well it uses its own material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities to the art's special material
rubrics_metrics.description: Each art ... has its own special responsibilities to its material. One of the functions of aesthetic criticism is to define these limitations; to estimate the degree in which a given work of art fulfils its responsibilities to its special material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics should identify the unique obligations a medium imposes (e.g., colour/line for painting, rhythm for poetry) and judge how fully the work meets them. Failure to consider medium-specific duties is a common critical error.

rubrics_metrics.name: True pictorial quality / pictorial charm
rubrics_metrics.description: To note in a picture that true pictorial charm, which is neither a mere poetical thought nor sentiment, on the one hand, nor a mere result of communicable technical skill in colour or design, on the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the presence of an essentially pictorial quality that sits between literary/poetic interest and mere technique. Look for inventive handling of line and colour that delights the senses directly rather than only conveying a poetic idea or technical virtuosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing (design) as an expression of pictorial temperament
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the drawing—the design projected from that peculiar pictorial temperament or constitution ... the arabesque traced in the air by Tintoret's flying figures, by Titian's forest branches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the drawing as the manifestation of a painter's pictorial temperament: compositional line, rhythm of forms, and the way shapes move through space. Examples given: Tintoretto's flying figures, Titian's branches. Poor drawing often betrays a lack of pictorial temperament even if proportions are anatomically correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colouring as essential pictorial quality
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the colouring—that weaving as of just perceptible gold threads of light through the dress, the flesh, the atmosphere ... the staining of the whole fabric of the thing with a new, delightful physical quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge how colouring creates atmosphere, texture, and a unifying physical quality in a painting. Examples: Titian's Lace-girl, Rubens's Descent from the Cross. Colour should operate beyond mere local truth to imbue the whole picture with a unique sensuous effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary requirement: delight the sense
rubrics_metrics.description: These essential pictorial qualities must first of all delight the sense, delight it as directly and sensuously as a fragment of Venetian glass; and through this delight only be the medium of whatever poetry or science may lie beyond them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A great picture's first success is sensuous delight—visual pleasure or wonder—before any intellectual or narrative meaning. If a work fails to delight sensuously, any poetic or didactic claims are diminished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subordination of subject to pictorial design
rubrics_metrics.description: The given person or subject ... is often merely the pretext for a kind of work which carries one quite out of the range of its conventional associations ... the subordination of mere subject to pictorial design, to the main purpose of a picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the painter uses subject matter as a starting-point for pictorial invention rather than as an end in itself. Good pictorial art may reshape or subordinate narrative elements for compositional or sensuous ends (Leonardo, Giorgione examples). Beware overly literal or merely illustrative treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art's aspiration to unity of form and matter (musical ideal)
rubrics_metrics.description: All art constantly aspires towards the condition of music ... the end is not distinct from the means, the form from the matter, the subject from the expression; they inhere in and completely saturate each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An important measure of excellence is how thoroughly form and content are fused: the painting's means (technique, colour, line) should be inseparable from its expressive end. The closer a work approaches this 'musical' ideal, the higher its artistic achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anders-streben: inter-art tendencies
rubrics_metrics.description: In its special mode of handling its given material, each art may be observed to pass into the condition of some other art, by what German critics term an Anders-streben—a partial alienation from its own limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise and evaluate successful cross-art influences (e.g., pictorial works that achieve musical-like unity or poetry that attains pictorial immediacy). Assess whether such borrowing strengthens or weakens the work's core pictorial obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of matter/form distinction (lyrical ideal)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ideal types of poetry are those in which this distinction is reduced to its minimum; so that lyrical poetry ... is, at least artistically, the highest and most complete form of poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging works that verge on lyricism, consider how minimising the separation between matter and form heightens artistic value. Applied to painting: value works where subject is vague or suppressed in favor of an informing pictorial mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pictorial handling of landscape and light
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes a momentary tint of stormy light may invest a homely or too familiar scene with a character which might well have been drawn from the deep places of the imagination ... hence the superiority, for most conditions of the picturesque, of a river-side in France to a Swiss valley.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate landscapes by how effectively light, atmosphere, and selective detail are used to transform ordinary material into an informing pictorial emotion. Consider local material conditions (topography, colour) and how a painter modulates them to a dominant tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Painting as decorative, ocular art (Venetian principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Those earlier Venetian painters ... seem never for a moment to have been tempted even to lose sight of the scope of their art in its strictness, or to forget that painting must be, before all things decorative, a thing for the eye; a space of colour on the wall ... this, to begin and end with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value works that prioritise pictorial cohesion, surface beauty, and decorative harmony appropriate to painting. The Venetian ideal emphasises the picture as an object of visual delight rather than primarily a vehicle for theological or philosophical content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pictorial invention/symbolical use of subject
rubrics_metrics.description: The ostensible subject is used, not as matter for definite pictorial realisation, but as the starting-point of a train of sentiment as subtle and vague as a piece of music ... subjects of sacred story not for their own sake, but as a symbolical language for fancies all his own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how inventively the artist uses subject-matter symbolically to summon moods or associations beyond literal narrative. Successful symbolic treatment produces nuanced, music-like effects; unsuccessful treatment may feel obscure or merely decorative without depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of new pictorial genres/forms (e.g., Giorgione's genre pictures)
rubrics_metrics.description: He is the inventor of genre, of those easily movable pictures which serve neither for uses of devotion, nor of allegorical or historic teaching—little groups of real men and women ... morsels of actual life, conversation or music or play, refined upon or idealised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating innovation, note whether an artist invents durable pictorial forms (new genres) that expand the medium's expressive range. Giorgione's invention of small 'genre' pictures is offered as a model of significant formal innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution/authenticity and its effect on evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Much of the work on which Giorgione's immediate fame depended ... work done for instantaneous effect, in all probability passed away almost within his own age ... it is now known that only one is certainly from Giorgione's hand. The accomplished science of the subject has ... assured us that we possess of it less than we seemed to possess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provenance and correct attribution are crucial to evaluating an artist's oeuvre and influence. Be wary of assessments based on misattributed works; recent critical scholarship can materially change reputations and judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taste for pictorial temper and avoidance of over-literalism
rubrics_metrics.description: To suppose that all is mere technical acquirement in delineation or touch, working through and addressing itself to the intelligence ... or a merely poetical, or literary interest, addressed also to the pure intelligence, on the other;—this is the way of most spectators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism should avoid reducing painting to either technique alone or to literary/poetic illustration. Give weight to the painter's pictorial temperament and the non-intellectual, sensuous aspects of art rather than only iconographic or textual readings.
